inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD flows; HKD is pegged to USD so the risk-free anchor is ~4.0% (HK 10y Exchange Fund ~3.6%, UST 10y ~4.2%). ERP 5.5% plus ~1.0% for PRC manufacturing/tariff exposure; levered beta ~1.2 for a highly cyclical commodity-electronics materials maker -> cost of equity ~11.8%. Bank debt at 2.8% pre-tax (interim note) is ~15% of capital at a through-cycle equity value -> WACC ~10.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and AI-capex concentration are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.

inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Kingboard Laminates is a vertically integrated copper-clad-laminate maker (CCL plus copper foil, e-glass yarn/fabric, epoxy, kraft paper) - an operating manufacturer whose value is a free-cash-flow stream, not a bank/REIT/holdco. No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry: fresh build. FY0 BASIS: revenue is TTM to 30 Jun 2026 for the Laminates and Properties segments only (Laminates FY25 20,225.3 + H1 FY26 14,774.8 - H1 FY25 9,496.9 = 25,503.2; Properties 77.6 + 48.6 - 43.9 = 82.3; total 25,585.5). The Investments segment (dividend and bond-coupon income booked as 'revenue', HK$80.4m in H1 FY26) is excluded from the flows and its source assets (equity instruments at FVTPL 2,954.5 + debt instruments at FVTOCI 256.4 = 3,210.9 at 30 Jun 2026) are in the equity bridge at fair value (matching-asset rule). Year 1 of the projection is therefore the twelve months to 30 Jun 2027, consistent with the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet. TTM Laminates EBITDA = FY25 3,676.6 + H1 FY26 4,336.3 - H1 FY25 ~1,606 = ~6,407 (25.1%); FY25 alone was 18.2%. last_fcf is FY2025 audited (reported FCF 883.2 = OCF 2,160.2 - capex 1,277.0; less bank interest income 14.1); the interim cash-flow statement is condensed and does not split capex out of HK$3,580m investing outflows (which include ~HK$1.4bn of securities purchases), so no TTM owner FCF is stated. AI-CYCLE JUDGMENT: H1 FY26 Laminates EBITDA margin 29.3% (vs 18.2% FY25) and a record July-2026 profit of ~HK$1.1bn (a ~HK$13bn annualised NPAT run-rate vs HK$2.4bn in FY25) are treated as a cyclical upswing driven by an e-glass yarn/fabric and HVLP copper-foil shortage, not a new steady state. The base case lets the boom run through year 1 (EBITDA margin 38%) and partly into year 2 (33%), then mean-reverts as industry capacity (including the group's own new kilns, Shaoguan yarn/fabric and the 2027 copper-foil plant) catches up: revenue falls 15% and 8% in years 3-4 and margin settles at 21.5-22%, versus a FY2018-FY2025 group average of ~21.7% and a range of 14%-32%. The normalised margin is set slightly above the historic average for the AI/high-end mix shift and below the FY2021 peak. buyback_cash 0: the company has never repurchased; the flat count is a modelling convention, not a funded policy. Price context: 52-week range HK$10.50-107.20; the stock ran from ~HK$12 to ~HK$98 (Jun-2026) and has since roughly halved.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.7%) diverges >30% from EPS 3yr (8.4%) and EPS 5yr (-3.0%) and revenue 3yr (-3.0%). Book value is suppressed by very high payouts (FY2021 HK$7.8bn and FY2022 HK$4.7bn dividends), and every series is dominated by where the endpoints fall in the CCL cycle (FY2020 trough-ish, FY2021 peak, FY2023 trough). None of these CAGRs is used as a driver; the projection is a cycle path, not a compounding rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - bank interest income): FY2020 1,549.1; FY2022 3,805.6; FY2025 869.1. Owner-FCF CAGRs are essentially identical to reported-FCF CAGRs (-11.0% 5yr, -39.0% 3yr) because SBC is near zero: the FCF decline is a capex-cycle and working-capital effect (FY2025 capex 1,277 as AI capacity was built; receivable days rose to 96), not stock comp. Endpoints sit at different points of the cycle, so these CAGRs describe the cycle, not a trend.

base.narrative: AI-driven shortage persists through H1 2027 then normalises; mid-cycle margin ~22% on a larger, richer-mix revenue base.
base.capex_pct_path_note: Year 1 ~HK$3.8bn: Shaoguan 70kt yarn / 96m-metre fabric plant (H2 FY26 start), Qingyuan low-Dk kilns, 21kt copper-foil plant for mid-2027; HK$1.22bn of PP&E deposits already paid at 30 Jun 2026. Steady-state 5.5% vs FY2018-25 average ~5.5%.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: Net working capital (inventory + trade/bills receivables + due from fellow subs - trade/bills payables - contract liabilities) ~HK$12.4bn at 30 Jun 2026, ~45% of annualised revenue; 126-day cycle. Growth consumes cash and the down-cycle releases it (FY2022 OCF 6.0bn vs NPAT 1.9bn).

bull.narrative: July-2026 run-rate holds for two years; AI-grade glass yarn/HVLP foil becomes a durable high-margin niche; mid-cycle margin resets to ~30%.

bear.narrative: Shortage clears within months as industry yarn/foil capacity lands and hyperscaler capex pauses; prices and copper roll over; margins revert to the FY2023-24 trough band with an over-built asset base.

scenario_narratives.base: The AI-server upcycle is real but cyclical. Kingboard's vertically integrated e-glass yarn/fabric and copper-foil chain lets it raise prices on both upstream materials and finished laminates while the shortage lasts, so the twelve months to June 2027 run at ~38% EBITDA margin on ~45% higher revenue, but below the July-2026 monthly peak. From 2027-28 the group's own new kilns, the Shaoguan yarn/fabric plant, its 2027 copper-foil plant and competitors' capacity (Taiwan, Japan and mainland e-glass makers) close the gap; laminate and yarn prices fall back and revenue drops ~22% over two years. The business then settles on a structurally larger, higher-mix base (AI servers, 800G switches, IC substrates, auto electronics) at a 22% mid-cycle EBITDA margin - slightly above its FY2018-25 average because of the high-end mix - growing 3-4%. Working capital consumes cash on the way up and releases it on the way down.
scenario_narratives.bull: Hyperscaler and sovereign AI capex keeps compounding, and low-Dk/low-CTE glass yarn and HVLP3 foil prove to be a genuine bottleneck that only a handful of certified suppliers can fill. Kingboard's early kiln investment and Tier-1 certifications let it hold ~42% EBITDA margins for two years and normalise only to ~30% (versus a historic 32% cycle peak) as the product mix permanently shifts up the value chain; revenue keeps growing with capacity additions. Exit at 14x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: The shortage is a classic double-ordering bubble: PCB makers built inventory ahead of an AI-capex pause, competitors' e-glass and copper-foil capacity lands in 2027, and copper prices roll over. Year-1 revenue grows only 25% before falling 20% and 10%; EBITDA margins return to the FY2023-24 trough band (14-16%) and settle at 17%, leaving the group over-built after HK$5bn+ of expansion capex, with US-China export-control and tariff escalation hitting PRC-made AI content and related-party Kingboard Holdings demand softening. Exit at 10x FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because earnings are at the top of an unusually sharp, AI-concentrated cycle in a business whose history is boom-bust (FY2021 peak to FY2023 trough: EBITDA -74%) and whose expansion is being funded with short-term debt; base 50% as the central mean-reversion path; bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things (sustained hyperscaler capex, no competitor capacity response, durable mix-shift pricing) to all go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the AI upcycle as a cash windfall, not a perpetuity. The base case capitalises a mid-cycle margin (~22%) on a larger, richer-mix revenue base after banking two boom years of cash; the market price, which sits above even the bull case, is capitalising something close to peak earnings.
key_risks_to_valuation: Duration of the e-glass yarn/fabric and copper-foil shortage: each extra boom year at ~38% rather than ~22% EBITDA margin adds roughly HK$1.5/share
Normalised margin: every 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth ~HK$0.8/share in the base case
Working capital: at ~45% of revenue, the WC drag on the way up (and release on the way down) dominates year-1 and year-3 FCF
US-China export controls/tariffs on AI hardware content made in the PRC
Related-party sales to Kingboard Holdings subsidiaries (~17% of H1 FY26 revenue) and family-controlled governance; KBCF minority litigation appeal
Short-term-heavy bank debt (84% due within a year) funding the capex programme
